Four equiprobable pairs of fair attempted outcomes produce three first-report successes when success completes earlier. The first stored success probability is 3/4 although each attempted success probability is 1/2. Every run is complete and accepted. S denotes success and R rejection.

In the fair 20-attempt model, the event of at least 10 successes has exact mass 308333/524288. Under success-first completion, that event makes the first 10 stored reports all successes and returns [3/5, 1], excluding the attempted parameter 1/2. This lower bound already exceeds alpha = 1/10. The complete count-class miss mass is 616667/1048576.

The source deadline example has two independent fair bits. The second report is available exactly when the first bit succeeds, a rule depending only on the past. Completion probability is 1/2, but first-bit success conditional on completion is 1. Unconditional issued-bad bounds therefore cannot be read as conditional guarantees.

The defined recorder uses one global operation-ID namespace. A matching completion removes the pending intent and appends one success, rejection or fault. Binary successes and rejections count once, while faults add no binary sample. Replays are idempotent and conflicts reject the command word.

In the exact four-command example, begin creates one pending operation, finish adds one successful sample, and both replayed finish and late begin leave terminal count 1 and pending count 0. Appending a conflicting rejection fails at zero-based command index 4.

The commit recovery model validates sequence, exact pre-state and post-state projections. A new matching receipt replays one checked logical transition. A duplicate acknowledgement preserves the checkpoint, budget and belief exactly. Physical atomic durable storage is an explicit backend obligation.
